sources.entry: Notable - The markdown-based note-taking app that doesn't suck.

summary.one_liner: Notable is a markdown-based note-taking app that stores notes as plain files on disk, uses GitHub Flavored Markdown with a VS Code-style editor, and offers a dark theme and zen mode.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes a note-taking app where notes are written in GitHub Flavored Markdown, with KaTeX math and Mermaid diagram support mentioned. The editor is said to be the same one VS Code uses, providing multi-cursor editing, a minimap and syntax highlighting. Notes and attachments are stored as ordinary files on the user's disk, so they can be edited with other editors, synced via Dropbox, or versioned with Git. It includes a split editor showing rendered output alongside source, a multi-note editor for bulk actions like favoriting, pinning, deleting and tagging, a dark theme, and a zen mode. The README also mentions a quick open window, keyboard-friendly navigation, and a planned command palette. The author's stated goals include tags that can nest indefinitely and importing Evernote notes, but the README does not confirm these as implemented features.
use_cases: take notes with math and diagrams
keep notes as plain files on disk
switch from Evernote to a markdown app
bulk tag or pin multiple notes
notable: Editor is the same one used by VS Code, with multi-cursor and minimap
Notes are plain files on disk with no proprietary format or vendor lock-in
Supports GitHub Flavored Markdown plus KaTeX and Mermaid
Multi-note editor for bulk actions on many notes at once
caveats: Only older versions of the app are open-source, according to the License section
Command palette and custom themes are described as future features
README does not list install instructions or supported platforms
